title: Authorizing AI Agents
subtitle: Guardrails at prompt, retrieval, and response
content:
🤖 Sara's Three Gates (Verified Pattern)

The reviewed PlainID LangChain pattern governs Sara (Tier-1 analyst, Germany) with three enforcement gates, each backed by the same policy plane:

  • Gate 1 — prompt categorization: her query product support + internal security is classified; internal_security is outside her allowed categories → denied before any retrieval.
  • Gate 2 — policy-aware retrieval: the retriever applies PDP filters (region eu-central) so US documents never enter context.
  • Gate 3 — response anonymization: reporter names (PII asset type) are masked in output per her policy.
Three gates: categorize, filter retrieval, anonymize response 
# Gate 1: categorize BEFORE processing (reviewed LangChain pattern)
category = categorizer.invoke(user_query)   # 'internal_security' -> DENY
# "You're not authorized to ask about these topics."

# Gate 2: retrieval already filtered by PDP (region eu-central only)
filtered_docs = plainid_retriever.invoke(user_query)

# Gate 3: PII masked on the way out (reporter names)
result = plainid_anonymizer.invoke(user_query)
# Gate 1: categorize BEFORE processing (reviewed LangChain pattern) category = categorizer.invoke(user_query) # 'internal_security' -> DENY # "You're not authorized to ask about these topics." # Gate 2: retrieval already filtered by PDP (region eu-central only) filtered_docs = plainid_retriever.invoke(user_query) # Gate 3: PII masked on the way out (reporter names) result = plainid_anonymizer.invoke(user_query)

🔍 Critical Review Notes

  • Gate order is load-bearing: categorizing after retrieval leaks unauthorized content into context (and logs). Deny early.
  • Retrieval filtering ≠ output filtering: region-gating decides which docs; anonymization decides which fields. Both gates stay; neither subsumes the other.
  • Agent identity is a first-class subject: multi-identity evaluation (human + agent + app, AND semantics) means the agent's clearance gates too — a cleared human driving an uncleared agent still denies.
  • MCP/tool calls are actions: every tool invocation is an (agent, action, resource) triple through the PDP — tools are the new API endpoints. No PlainID tenant? The same triple gates through OPA (allow if input.agent.clearance >= input.tool.sensitivity over a tool-allowlist) or Cedar (permit per tool action + forbid on exfil compositions) — the gates are architecture, not vendor.

⛔ Enforcement Limits (Read Before Trusting the Gates)

  • Gate 1 is probabilistic: the categorizer is an LLM classifier — paraphrase and prompt injection bypass it. Require allowlist categories, an adversarial test set, and human approval for high-risk tools. Adversarial set, minimum (run on every categorizer change): 5 paraphrases of each blocked topic, 3 injection probes (ignore previous instructions…, role-play, encoding tricks), 3 mixed allowed+blocked queries — all must deny. (Per docs, the categorizer also supports a single identity per request — do not assume multi-identity framing everywhere.)
  • Blocked answers still leak: retrieved-then-blocked content touches context, logs, caches, and embeddings. Gate order reduces but does not eliminate retention — scope sessions and audit tool I/O.
  • Anonymization ≠ de-identification: masked names re-identify via joins and aggregates. Treat anonymizer output as pseudonymized, not anonymous.
  • Composed allowed actions leak: allowed search + allowed email = exfiltration. AND-semantics across identities does not stop two individually-permitted steps from composing into one violation — model dangerous compositions explicitly.
  • PDP-per-call has a price: latency, invoice volume, and fail-closed availability all scale with tool-call counts. Deny on PIP-unavailable by default; enabling skipUnneededOrUnavailableIdentitySources-style leniency is an explicitly risk-accepted decision, logged per call.
  • TOCTOU sessions: policy or attributes changing mid-session must re-gate open tool loops — a verdict at turn 1 is not a verdict at turn 20.
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Walk Sara’s request through the three gates; change topic, region, PII. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: Sara asks about product support AND internal security. What happens at Gate 1?

options.text: Denied before retrieval — internal_security is outside her allowed categories
Allowed — any support keyword suffices
Allowed but logged silently
The agent answers from memory instead

questions.explanation: Categorization gates the whole interaction. Mixed queries containing restricted topics deny — partial compliance is non-compliance.

questions.question: Why must categorization run BEFORE retrieval?

options.text: Otherwise unauthorized content enters context/logs even if the final answer is blocked
It makes responses faster
Retrieval requires a category label to function
Order does not matter

questions.explanation: Late gates leak: retrieved-then-blocked content still touched the model, the logs, and possibly the cache. Deny early.

questions.question: Region filter allows eu-central docs; reporter names still show raw. Which gate is missing?

options.text: Response anonymization (field-level PII masking on output)
Prompt categorization
JWT verification
DNS filtering

questions.explanation: Retrieval gates documents; anonymization gates fields. The reviewed pattern keeps both — region ≠ de-identification.

questions.question: A cleared human tasks an uncleared support agent with reading restricted cases. Verdict under multi-identity AND?

options.text: Deny — every identity (human, agent, app) must satisfy its template's rules
Allow — the human's clearance covers the agent
Allow — agents inherit human rights
Allow on weekdays

questions.explanation: AND semantics close the confused-deputy gap: the weakest identity in the chain gates the decision.

questions.question: An agent calls delete-customer-record via an MCP tool. How should this be authorized?

options.text: As (agent, delete, customer-record) through the PDP — tools are actions on resources
Tool calls are internal and need no authorization
Allow all tool calls for speed
Only authorize the first tool call per session

questions.explanation: Every tool invocation crosses a trust boundary. PDP-per-call with the agent as subject is the reviewed posture.

questions.question: A tool result containing injected instructions arrives mid-session. Which gate applies?

options.text: Treat tool output as untrusted input — re-categorize before acting on it
Trust all tool output implicitly
Skip gates once a session is open
Allow everything tools return

questions.explanation: Retrieved content is the oldest injection vector in the new stack. Gates re-apply at every trust boundary, including tool returns.

questions.question: The support-bot needs broader access than Sara for one debugging session. Safe pattern?

options.text: Time-boxed elevation with approval and full tool-I/O audit, auto-expiring
Permanent elevation for convenience
Share Sara's personal token
Disable the PDP for the session

questions.explanation: Exceptional access is normal; permanent exceptional access is a backdoor. Box it in time, approval, and audit.

questions.question: An allowlisted category name appears inside attacker-quoted text. Handling?

options.text: Classify intent and structure, not keywords — quoted payload is data, not instruction
Allow — the keyword matched
Deny all quoted text everywhere
Strip quotes and re-check keywords

questions.explanation: Keyword gates fall to quoting. Categorization must separate instruction from payload, or attackers will supply the keywords.
